run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:50:03Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504s that frontend-proxy returned on its 'ingress' server spans after the single Kafka broker was deliberately restarted at 2026-11-15T04:47:32Z. Ingress error spans rose from ~1.41 per 735s at window start to 182-228 per 735s by ~04:56-04:57 (188.5 at the last point), and the error share of ingress spans went from 0-0.35% before ~04:47 to 1.5% at ~04:50 and 3.0-4.2% from 04:52 through 05:01, so the condition was still present at the window end. Each failing span is a 504 lasting ~15.000s, while the corresponding frontend 'POST /api/checkout' spans ran past the proxy deadline (15.4s and 21.6s) and returned HTTP 200; inside checkout the dominant child is 'orders publish' (15.2s and 21.3s of 15.4s and 21.5s PlaceOrder), i.e. the Kafka produce. The same checkout spans took 150-200ms before the restart. The Kafka pod was recreated by its Deployment (new ReplicaSet revision 2, pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 created 04:47:32Z, restartCount 0, identical template, annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=04:47:32Z, no data volume); checkout logged 'connection refused' to kafka:9092 from 04:48:52 to 04:49:04 plus 'circuit breaker is open', and the broker came back with an empty log ('orders-0 ... from offset 0 ... high watermark 0'). Why produces still took 15-21s after the broker rejoined at ~04:49:17 is not established: Kafka has no metrics here, its logs show no ERROR/WARN after startup, and its CPU (0.009-0.024 cores of a 400m limit) and throttling (~0.5-1.6%) were low. frontend recorded zero error spans; the failure surfaced as checkout latency and proxy-side timeouts.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error signal is confined to its server span 'ingress': STATUS_CODE_ERROR increased from ~1.41 spans per 735s at window start to 144.9-227.9 by ~04:56-04:57 (188.5 at the last point), while the client span 'router frontend egress' had STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 at every point. The status_code label listing for the service returns only STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

The failing frontend-proxy spans are HTTP 504s with a duration of about 15.000s: sampled error spans on operation 'ingress' carry {error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR} with durations 14,999,928-15,001,259 us, and in the same traces the child 'router frontend egress' spans last 15,000,488-15,009,105 us with error="true" and http.status_code="0".

Trace 8ebb654aa5b3473caa81840f4b2113d6 shows the failure path: load-generator span 'POST' 504 at 15.002s -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 at 15.001s -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' completing with http.status_code 200 at 15.444s -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 15.440s, whose dominant child 'orders publish' took 15.237s. Other spans in the same trace (cart 200-347us, currency 431-53,171us, product-catalog 86-479us, payment 288-544us, shipping 27-1,923us, quote 26-306us, email 3,494-72,219us) returned grpc status 0 / HTTP 200 in milliseconds.

Trace 0525cd2c7ae0209858a8b500fd24cabc shows the same pattern at larger magnitude: checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 21.477s of which child 'orders publish' is 21.330s, frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 21.571s with http.status_code 200, frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 at 15.001s, load-generator 'POST' 504 at 15.002s; payment charge 706us and all other callees are sub-100ms.

In the 30-row slice of the 414 frontend spans of 10s or longer returned for 04:56-05:02, every row belongs to the checkout path: 'POST /api/checkout' (15.7-21.6s), 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (15.4-21.5s) and the frontend 'POST' child (15.0s); durations reach 21.57s, well past the 15s at which frontend-proxy records a 504.

Baseline before the Kafka restart: frontend 'POST /api/checkout' spans in 04:30-04:44 were 150,975-199,057us and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 105,527-191,895us, all http.status_code 200 / grpc status 0.

Kafka was restarted by its Deployment at 04:47:32Z: pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 has creationTimestamp 2026-11-15T04:47:32Z, owner ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485, container 'kafka' started 04:47:33Z with restartCount 0 and lastState {}; events at 04:47:32-04:47:34Z are SuccessfulCreate of kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97, ScalingReplicaSet kafka 0->1, SuccessfulDelete of kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 and Killing of that pod.

The Kafka restart changed nothing in the pod template: ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 (deployment revision 1) and kafka-5c9d7cc485 (revision 2) carry the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, identical env, identical resources (limits cpu 400m / memory 900Mi) and no volumes; only the new ReplicaSet has annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T04:47:32Z. The running Kafka pod mounts no data volume, only the projected service-account token.

The restarted broker came up with no prior state: Kafka logs record '[QuorumController id=1] No previous registration found for broker 1' at 04:49:07Z and '[Broker id=1] Leader orders-0 ... starts at leader epoch 0 from offset 0 ... high watermark 0, ISR [1] ... Previous leader None' at 04:49:13Z, i.e. the orders topic was recreated empty.

The checkout pod's own logs show it lost Kafka during the restart: 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused' and 'client/metadata no available broker to send metadata request to' repeatedly between 04:48:52 and 04:49:04, 'Failed to write message: kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to' at 04:49:04, and 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open' between 04:48:46 and 04:49:14, followed by 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092' and 'producer/leader/orders/0 selected broker 1' at 04:49:17.

The frontend-proxy error burst starts with the Kafka restart: per-180s increase of 'ingress' error spans is 0-7.2 from ~04:33 through ~04:47, then 22.8, 43.2, 66.0, 36.7, 66.0, 47.3, 75.6, 74.4, 63.6, 79.2, 73.2, 63.9, 40.7 through 05:01; the 'router frontend egress' error series stays 0 at every point.

The error share of frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans was 0-0.0035 (0-0.35%) before ~04:47, rose to 0.0153 at ~04:50 and stayed 0.0265-0.0415 (2.7-4.2%) from ~04:52 to 05:01, so the condition was still present at the end of the window.

Within checkout, the only span with recorded errors is 'orders publish': STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 17.13 in the 735s window ending ~04:51 and 15.15 in the next, 0 in the latest window; every other checkout operation (oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, CartService/GetCart, CartService/EmptyCart, PaymentService/Charge, CurrencyService/Convert, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, HTTP POST) appears only as STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Kafka pod resource telemetry does not show saturation during the degraded period: CPU usage is 0.009-0.024 cores after ~04:52 (limit 400m), the CFS throttled-period ratio falls from 1.0/0.995 in the first post-start periods to 0.005-0.016 after ~04:52, and working set grows from 283,979,776 to 621,797,376 bytes against a 900Mi limit.

Other cluster state around the alert: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready, and kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 is the only pod started at 04:47:32Z (siblings started 04:14-04:16Z); all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

A separate failure observed on a different entity: the fraud-detection container in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm has restartCount 2 and lastState.terminated {reason: OOMKilled, exitCode: 137, startedAt 04:36:38Z, finishedAt 04:40:37Z}, with a BackOff warning event at 04:40:38Z, preceding the Kafka rollout by about seven minutes.

Most likely cause: the deliberate restart of the single Kafka broker at 04:47:32Z is the origin of the frontend-proxy error rate. The restart took the broker down (checkout 'connection refused' 04:48:52-04:49:04, circuit breaker open) and wiped its non-persistent log (orders-0 recreated at offset 0/high watermark 0), after which checkout's 'orders publish' produce spans took 15.2-21.3s instead of baseline milliseconds, pushing frontend 'POST /api/checkout' to 15-21.6s, beyond the ~15.000s deadline at which frontend-proxy ends its egress span and returns 504; those 504s are the error spans that raised RequestErrorRate.

Unresolved sub-question: why order publishes still took 15-21s after the broker rejoined at ~04:49:17. Candidate explanations the evidence cannot separate are (a) broker-side post-restart catch-up for the recreated topics and consumer-group re-registration and (b) producer-side retry/backoff still recovering from the outage. Kafka CPU was low (0.009-0.024 cores), throttling ~0.5-1.6%, memory 622MB of 900Mi, and its logs contain no ERROR/WARN after startup, so resource saturation is not supported; broker request latency cannot be measured here.

frontend itself is not recording errors: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase is 0 at every point in the window, and in the examined traces its checkout spans return http.status_code 200 (at 15.4s and 21.6s) while the proxy has already returned 504. frontend-proxy and checkout pods show no local resource change either: frontend-proxy CFS throttling is 2.3-4.6% both before and during the incident and checkout is 0% throughout, so proxy/host CPU is not what changed.

Rejected: the fraud-detection OOMKill at 04:40:37Z as the cause of this alert. It happened about seven minutes before the Kafka restart and before the error-rate step at ~04:47-04:50, and the checkout traces examined contain no fraud-detection span on the request path, so nothing ties it to the frontend-proxy 504s; it remains a separate, self-evidenced failure of that pod.

Rejected: a change in frontend-proxy's own configuration or resources as the trigger. Its pod was not recreated (started 04:14:29Z, 0 restarts), no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in otel-demo (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, product-catalog-products), and its CPU throttling is unchanged across the incident; the 504s coincide exactly with upstream responses exceeding its ~15s deadline.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what issued the Kafka rollout restart at 04:47:32Z cannot be established; only the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T04:47:32Z and the deployment revision 1->2 are visible.

No Kafka-specific metrics exist in this Prometheus: a metric-name search for .*kafka.* returned no_data (669941af-e602-45fd-96ef-4f37d59d2d80-t0:2d6e6b99-6366-4356-9d48-cb88e0c6de89) and a series search for service_name="kafka" returned no_data (06ac5d1c-bd52-48e9-8b95-07e281b0b769-t0:a9d27e6a-20a9-4539-8054-6ea1e8167d10), so broker produce/fetch latency, queue time, disk I/O and consumer lag are unknown, not zero.

The alert rule RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data, 9de3ad2f-9461-4721-9333-cecbee5ec864-t0:5e4da3d2-7d38-443b-9f3e-9ab57c4a56d3), so the exact alert expression and the annotation value 'current: 0.39999999999999997' could not be reproduced or tied to a specific metric.

Jaeger retention for this target ends around 2026-11-15T04:58:46Z, so there are no traces for the final ~4 minutes of the window; the persistence of 15-21s produce latency after 04:58 is visible only through span metrics and error ratios, not traces.

frontend-proxy's ~15s deadline is inferred from span timing (egress span ends at 15,000,488-15,009,105 us with http.status_code=0) because its Envoy configuration is baked into the image and no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in otel-demo; the literal timeout setting could not be read.

Consumer-side impact of the Kafka data loss was not verified: accounting logs returned no_data for the filtered read (8c517cf0-474a-4d8a-850f-b43343d87c20-t1:1484dd66-5283-4d6a-9b5a-ca64b2987890), and fraud-detection and other consumer logs were not read, so whether accounting or fraud-detection lost or reprocessed orders is unknown.

Several other checks returned no_data and are therefore unknown rather than clear: rpc_client_duration_milliseconds for frontend (7882a23b-6406-4195-b5c8-8c26cf71e355-t1:2009d4ef-e419-4b95-964d-a3463a568595), http_server_request_duration_seconds labels (fc726c68-31ab-47aa-a50b-9fb0e6cadf7b-t0:572927b6-c7b3-4ea3-bef7-e333eaeacb33), load-generator ERROR spans (03f71739-d2be-4b5a-bbee-e3e2745ab24c-t0:0c630616-e355-4679-a4df-e153cb4c24d5, b4773be6-bb9a-4811-a6ab-f3c2538c16fe-t1:40e74cf4-365c-496f-94a0-826768497b5e), a frontend-proxy ConfigMap lookup (8ac7e812-7e63-4068-a16c-cf7cd65c2afa-t2:714086f7-3c3f-4398-a792-63e3a56051a9), and a late 'orders publish' trace search (50c150fe-bfa6-4b22-9aa6-d7aa6767829a-t1:1db72761-f189-4e76-b652-216eee2bf119).
The image-provider, ad and recommendation services, and frontend routes other than /api/checkout, were not examined; they are unassessed rather than cleared.
next_steps: Confirm with the platform or change owner why the Kafka Deployment was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-15T04:47:32Z, using the change-history system that is not integrated here.
Give the single Kafka broker persistent storage (or a PVC) so a restart does not wipe the orders topic and consumer offsets, and treat a restart of this broker as a data-affecting event.

Re-check Kafka produce latency after the broker settles; if publishes remain 15-21s, capture broker-side produce/purgatory metrics and disk latency on node i-0caf4b73702b2641e to decide between post-restart catch-up and producer retry/backoff.

Reconcile frontend-proxy's upstream deadline with checkout's worst-case latency (raise the ~15s proxy timeout above the observed 21.6s PlaceOrder time, or bound the Kafka produce timeout) so slow publishes do not surface as HTTP 504s.
Add Kafka broker and client metrics to the monitored target, since Kafka currently has no metrics or trace series and its health can only be inferred indirectly.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

notes: Container kafka has no previous instance (HTTP 400: previous terminated container "kafka" in pod "kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97" not found); the other streams are unaffected.
